department: Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering

deadline.value: Applications are accepted all year, but apply early: the department says applying by October for the following October improves your chance of a funding nomination. Awards panels meet in November, January, March and June. The President's PhD Scholarship rounds close 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027 and 1 Mar 2027.
deadline.quote: Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 2 November 2026 and are awarded a scholarship will be notified by 31 January 2027. | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 11 January 2027 | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 1 March 2027

also.quote: PhD applications are accepted throughout the year. However, applicants seeking scholarship funding are encouraged to apply as early as possible.
Applicants who apply earlier (i.e. by October for the following October), are more likely to be nominated for this funding as the process is highly competitive.

supervisor.value: If you propose your own project, you must discuss it with a potential supervisor before you apply. For an advertised studentship, the supervisor is the academic who holds the funding.
supervisor.quote: You will need to discuss your research idea with a potential supervisor before you apply.

funding.value: Supervisors nominate applicants for department, EPSRC and college funding only after an offer, and an Awards Panel decides. Some scholarships (Maria Petrou, Alex Fortescue) cover Home or Overseas fees for any nationality, but competition is intense: past winners typically had first-class master's degrees and publications.
funding.quote: Candidates are nominated by their potential PhD supervisor only after receiving an offer of a PhD place. | Previous successful applicants have obtained 1st class equivalent degrees at Master's level

also.quote: The Alex Fortescue scholarship covers tuition fees (Home & Overseas), bursary (at UKRI rates with London allowance) and an allowance towards conferences and travel.

entry_route.value: International applicants need the equivalent of a UK 2:1 bachelor's in electrical engineering or a related subject and the equivalent of a UK master's at Merit (or a UK-style integrated MEng at 2:1).
entry_route.quote: The equivalent of a UK 2.1 in a Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or a related subject AND the equivalent of a UK Master's degree at Merit.

toefl_min.value: EEE requires Imperial's Higher English level: TOEFL iBT 100 overall (min 22 in each section), or 5.0 on the new scale.
toefl_min.quote: To study with us all applicants must demonstrate they meet the required Higher English language competency level.

ielts_min.value: EEE requires Imperial's Higher English level: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall (min 6.5 in each element).
ielts_min.quote: To study with us all applicants must demonstrate they meet the required Higher English language competency level.

notes: The department admits 40-50 PhD students a year from around 350 applicants. Interviews with the potential supervisor are held on Teams, and a decision usually comes within 8 weeks. Funding does not cover visa or IHS fees.
